change_summary: PR #144 closes the single-command contributor bootstrap: repo-local oya wrapper, direnv PATH, Claude/Codex/Gemini/Hermes advisory hooks, install/uninstall scripts, validation/sync workflows, and vendored addyosmani/agent-skills with Oyatie overlay precedence.

review_history.summary: Initial combined reviewer found blockers in empty Claude settings, missing direnv PATH_add, destructive local --sync-skills semantics, post-sync validation, and INHERITANCE workflow-failure wording.

Re-review confirmed all previous blockers resolved: project-scoped Claude hooks populated, PATH_add bin present, local --sync-skills non-destructive, sync workflow validates newly downloaded tree before PR creation, and inheritance/provenance wording is consistent.

findings: The bootstrap uses repo-local files and a single install/uninstall path rather than adding user-level global state or parallel setup channels.
The first reviewer-agent pass found real bad-smell blockers; the final patch removed those special cases rather than explaining them away.
Vendor drift uses review PRs, never auto-merge, and now validates the newly downloaded tree plus Oyatie inheritance metadata before PR creation.
The bootstrap remains reproducible from the repository: wrapper, hooks, completions, docs, workflow, and vendored skills are all committed.
Adversarial review intentionally failed the first pass on empty Claude hooks, destructive sync semantics, missing post-sync validation, and PATH drift; those blockers were fixed before approval.
Hook scripts are encouragement-only and exit 0, so bad or unavailable local tools do not block agent autonomy.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: No previous blocker remains after fixes.

findings: New contributors can clone, run ./tools/hook-bootstrap/install.sh, and receive repo-scoped CLI/hook/skill setup without modifying home-directory agent configs.
.envrc now actually executes PATH_add bin, matching the documented oya wrapper ergonomics.
The combined reviewer-agent approved after blockers were closed and reported install.sh syntax plus vendored skill validation passing.
Committed Claude settings now carry the oya-bootstrap-v1 marker and concrete hook commands instead of an empty object.

alternatives_named: Require every contributor to install skills and hooks into ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, or ~/.hermes manually
Vendor agent-skills in-repo with Oyatie overlay precedence and project-scoped hook configs
Use a blocking hook model for canonical primitive enforcement
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Repo-vendored skills plus project-scoped, encouragement-only hooks satisfy reproducibility and avoid user-home residue; CI/admission remains the enforcement layer.
rejected_reasons: User-level manual installs are not reproducible from git clone and create hidden state.
Blocking hooks would violate the encouragement-over-prevention doctrine captured in the PR design amendment.

findings: Static scan of added non-vendor lines found no hardcoded secrets, shell injection, eval/exec, pickle, or SQL formatting patterns.
Install/uninstall paths are project-scoped and explicitly avoid ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.hermes, ~/.local/bin, and shell-profile mutation.
Hooks are short shell suggesters and advisory only; they do not add blocking build/test work to normal tool execution.
Workflow validation is scoped to hook/skill/bootstrap paths, avoiding broad workspace rebuilds for vendor-only changes.
This evidence file and matching audit-chain row close the contract-path requirement for PR #144.
The PR body Code Review section points to reviewer-agent verdict, resolved blockers, deferred follow-ups, and this evidence path.
The change is isolated to repo-local bootstrap files, workflows, docs, and vendored skill assets; rollback is a normal revert and uninstall.sh removes managed project hook files by marker.
Sync workflow emits explicit review PRs for upstream drift; bootstrap scripts print planned actions in dry-run and managed markers in generated configs.
No existing user-level agent setup is migrated or mutated. Adoption is additive and project-scoped, and uninstall round-trips managed project files only.
Bootstrap files use explicit hook-bootstrap, agent-skills, and oya-bootstrap-v1 names; queued oya git rename remains deferred outside this PR.
docs/bootstrap.md documents install/uninstall, project-scoped state, supported agent surfaces, validation workflows, and the no-user-home guarantee.
CLI wrapper, completions, hooks, hook-bootstrap scripts, workflows, and vendored skills live in separate, discoverable repo paths.
Oyatie authority overlays vendored upstream doctrine; docs/AGENTS.md and tools/agent-skills/INHERITANCE.md preserve Oyatie-wins precedence.
No new Cargo runtime dependency is introduced; external agent-skills content is vendored with MIT license and pinned upstream commit provenance.
UPSTREAM.json carries upstream metadata plus Oyatie-authored preservation fields; sync workflow validates those fields before creating drift PRs.
The sync algorithm preserves Oyatie-authored files/fields, replaces upstream-managed content, validates structure, then opens a review PR instead of mutating silently.
Assumption challenged: 'green CI is enough.' Resolution: contract path required reviewer-agent evidence and audit-chain coverage, and initial review findings were fixed before merge consideration.
The PR strengthens high-throughput agentic development by making the contributor environment reproducible while keeping Foundry/Oyatie doctrine authoritative over vendored generic skills.
